unmapped_findings: The paper addresses two steel classes: SIMPLEX low-density TWIP steels (25–30 wt.% Mn, <4–5 wt.% Al, or <8 wt.% Al when naturally aged) and κ-carbide strengthened austenitic steels (higher Al; κ-carbides form at 500–600 °C or during quenching for >10 wt.% Al).
As-cast RAP samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; after hot rolling and water quenching, a fully recrystallized ~20 μm grain structure with some retained Mn microsegregations was obtained.
Some alloys with up to 13 wt.% Al were synthesized for weight measurements, giving about 18% density reduction.
Thin-strip casting with in-line hot rolling was successfully conducted as a small-scale manufacturing pathway.
Ferritic low-density steels (Mn <8, Al 5–8, C <0.3 wt.%) and duplex austenite+ferrite grades (Mn 5–30, Al 3–10, C 0.1–0.7 wt.%) are mentioned for context.
κ-carbides are L'12-type ordered (Fe,Mn)3AlC non-oxide perovskites with <3% lattice mismatch to the austenitic matrix (and about -6% in a ferritic matrix).
